questions.text:
Let [latex] T(n) [/latex] be the recurrence relation defined as follows:
[latex] \begin{aligned} & T(0)=1, \\ & T(1)=2, \text { and } \\ & T(n)=5 T(n-1)-6 T(n-2) \text { for } n \geq 2 \end{aligned} [/latex]
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Characteristic equation: [latex]r^2-5r+6=0\Rightarrow r=2,3[/latex].
[latex]T(n)=\alpha2^n+\beta3^n[/latex]

[latex]T(0)=1:\ \alpha+\beta=1[/latex]
[latex]T(1)=2:\ 2\alpha+3\beta=2[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\beta=0,\ \alpha=1[/latex], so [latex]T(n)=2^n[/latex] (check: [latex]T(2)=10-6=4[/latex] True).

Answer: [latex]T(n)=\Theta(2^n)[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following recurrence relation:
[latex] T(n)=\left\{\begin{array}{c} \sqrt{n} T(\sqrt{n})+n \text { for } n \geq 1, \\ 1 \quad \text { for } n=1 . \end{array}\right. [/latex]
Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Divide both sides by [latex]n[/latex]: [latex]\frac{T(n)}{n}=\frac{T(\sqrt n)}{\sqrt n}+1[/latex].

Let [latex]S(n)=\frac{T(n)}{n}[/latex]. Then [latex]S(n)=S(\sqrt n)+1[/latex].

Taking square roots repeatedly, [latex]n\to n^{1/2}\to n^{1/4}\to\cdots[/latex] reaches a constant after [latex]\log\log n[/latex] steps, adding 1 each step. So [latex]S(n)=\Theta(\log\log n)[/latex].

[latex]T(n)=n\,S(n)=\Theta(n\log\log n)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]T(n)=\Theta(n\log\log n)[/latex]

questions.text:
The number of spanning trees in a complete graph of 4 vertices labelled A, B, C,
and D is _________
questions.solution:
Number of spanning trees of a complete graph [latex]K_n[/latex] (Cayley's formula) [latex]=n^{n-2}[/latex].

[latex]4^{4-2}=16[/latex]

Answer: 16

questions.text:
Given an integer array of size [latex]N[/latex], we want to check if the array is sorted (in either
ascending or descending order). An algorithm solves this problem by making a
single pass through the array and comparing each element of the array only with its
adjacent elements. The worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is
questions.solution:
The algorithm compares each pair of adjacent elements once: [latex]N-1[/latex] comparisons in the worst case (when the array is actually sorted, it must check every pair before saying YES).

It cannot do less: any element not examined could break the order. So the worst case is [latex]\Theta(N)[/latex], i.e. both [latex]O(N)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(N)[/latex].

Answer: both [latex]O(N)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(N)[/latex]

questions.text:
Let [latex]U = \{1, 2, 3\}[/latex]. Let [latex]2^U[/latex] denote the powerset of [latex]U[/latex]. Consider an undirected graph [latex]G[/latex] whose vertex set is [latex]2^U[/latex]. For any [latex]A,B \in 2^U, (A,B)[/latex] is an edge in [latex]G[/latex] if and only if (i) [latex]A \neq B[/latex], and (ii) either [latex]A \subseteq B[/latex] or [latex]B \subseteq A[/latex]. For any vertex [latex]A[/latex] in [latex]G[/latex], the set of all possible orderings in which the vertices of [latex]G[/latex] can be visited in a Breadth First Search (BFS) starting from [latex]A[/latex] is denoted by [latex]B(A)[/latex].
If [latex]\phi [/latex] denotes the empty set, then the cardinality of [latex]B(\phi ) [/latex] is ____.
questions.solution:
[latex]\phi[/latex] is a subset of every set, so [latex]\phi[/latex] is adjacent to all the other [latex]2^3-1=7[/latex] vertices.

BFS from [latex]\phi[/latex] visits all 7 neighbours at level 1, and these 7 can be visited in any order: [latex]7!=5040[/latex].

Answer: 5040
